title: Places and journeys
job: Tell a trip, directions and all
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedTenses: passato prossimo on essere, L2-M10's auxiliary law, for every step of the journey
passato prossimo on avere, L1-M5's, for what you did rather than where you went
present indicative, for the duration frame and for a departure still ahead
imperativo tu, L4-M1's, for directions given inside a story rather than at a counter

rules.text: MOTION VERBS ON essere, AT LENGTH. partire, arrivare, tornare, salire, scendere and the reflexive fermarsi all take essere, and their participle agrees with the SUBJECT: siamo partiti, siamo partite, mi sono fermato, mi sono persa. This is L2-M10's auxiliary law getting the workout it was written for — nothing new is being claimed, only used at length. The test is still the same one: a verb that moves you, or moves you into a state, goes on essere and its participle then behaves like an adjective.

partire da AND partire per POINT AT OPPOSITE ENDS OF THE SAME JOURNEY. partiamo da Milano is we leave FROM Milan; partiamo per Milano is we leave FOR Milan. The preposition carries the direction and the verb carries none of it, so a learner who drops the preposition has said nothing about which end they mean. English leave does the same trick with for and from, but English can also say we left Milan with no preposition at all, and Italian cannot.

THE DURATION FRAME, WHERE THE VERB AGREES WITH THE TIME. ci vuole un'ora, ci vogliono due ore. English it takes two hours has a dummy it for a subject; Italian's real subject is the HOURS, so the verb goes plural when they do. A learner who says ci vuole due ore has translated the dummy and left the verb behind. Same frame, same rule, for anything you can count: ci vuole un biglietto, ci vogliono due biglietti.

THE DIRECTIONS ARE ALREADY PAID FOR AND ONLY THE REGISTER MOVES. L2-M4 taught a destra, a sinistra, dritto, semaforo, ponte, angolo, strada and the rest in the Lei imperative, because there a stranger was asking a stranger. Told to a friend inside a story that is already running, the same directions come out in tu (gira a destra) or as a plain past (abbiamo girato a destra). The words do not change; the ending does, and that is the entire difference.

WHAT THIS MODULE POINTS AT AND LEAVES ALONE. Attached pronouns of place — andarci, arrivarci, restarci — wait for L5 with the rest of clitic attachment, so a journey here says al lago and never andarci. ne as a partitive is still unowned across the whole ladder and L4 leaves it that way on purpose. And the passato remoto of travel writing waits with the rest of the written past.

sentences.display: Siamo partiti presto e siamo arrivati a mezzogiorno
sentences.cue: We left early and we arrived at midday
sentences.literal: We-are left early and we-are arrived at midday

words.note: partire on essere, so the participle agrees with us: partiti for a group with any man in it, partite for a group of women.

sentences.trap: Both halves take essere and both participles agree. abbiamo partito is the single commonest error an English speaker makes with this verb.
sentences.sound: SYA-mo par-TEE-tee PRES-to e SYA-mo ar-ree-VA-tee a med-zo-JOR-no.

variations.display: Siamo partiti presto e siamo arrivati tardi
variations.cue: We left early and we arrived late
variations.changed: how the day went

variations.display: Siamo partiti presto, ma siamo arrivati tardi
variations.cue: We left early, but we arrived late
variations.changed: ma making the point of the sentence

variations.display: Siamo partiti a mezzogiorno e siamo arrivati di sera
variations.cue: We left at midday and we arrived in the evening
variations.changed: the whole trip shifted later

mistake.display: Abbiamo partito presto e abbiamo arrivato a mezzogiorno
mistake.why: partire and arrivare go on essere. The auxiliary is siamo and the participle agrees with the travellers: siamo partiti, siamo arrivati.

sentences.usage: The first line of the answer to how the journey was.
sentences.mnemonic: You go on essere, so the ending follows you.

sentences.display: Ci vogliono due ore per arrivare al lago
sentences.cue: It takes two hours to get to the lake
sentences.literal: There want two hours for to-arrive at-the lake

words.note: Plural because its subject is the HOURS. Anything countable behind it takes this form: ci vogliono due ore, ci vogliono due biglietti.
un'ora carries its elision as one word. Feminine, so due ore and not due ori, and it is what the duration frame agrees with.
The infinitive behind L3-M10's arrivati. After per it is the ordinary way of saying in order to get somewhere.
The plural takes an h to keep the g hard: laghi, LA-ghee. Al lago is where you go, as al mare is.

sentences.trap: English it takes has a dummy subject and Italian's subject is real. Two hours is plural, so the verb is ci vogliono and never ci vuole.
sentences.sound: chee VO-lyo-no DOO-e O-re per ar-ree-VA-re al LA-go. vogliono is stressed early, VO-lyo-no.

variations.display: Ci vogliono tre ore per arrivare al lago
variations.cue: It takes three hours to get to the lake
variations.changed: how long

variations.display: Ci vogliono due ore per arrivare al mare
variations.cue: It takes two hours to get to the sea
variations.changed: where you are going

variations.display: Ci vogliono due ore in macchina
variations.cue: It takes two hours by car
variations.changed: the destination dropped and the means added

mistake.display: Ci vuole due ore per arrivare al lago
mistake.why: This is the English dummy subject translated straight across. The hours are the subject in Italian, so the verb goes plural with them.

sentences.usage: Answering somebody who is deciding whether the trip is worth it.
sentences.mnemonic: The hours are the subject, so the hours pick the verb.

sentences.display: Ci vuole un'ora per arrivare in aereo
sentences.cue: It takes an hour to get there by plane
sentences.literal: There wants an-hour for to-arrive in plane

words.note: Singular because one hour is singular. It is not about the traveller at all: ci vuole un'ora whether one of you goes or ten.
In aereo, in treno, in macchina — the means of travel takes in with no article, exactly as L2-M4's in macchina does.

sentences.trap: The verb agrees with the time and never with the people travelling. Ten of you still say ci vuole un'ora.
sentences.sound: chee VWO-le oo-NO-ra per ar-ree-VA-re een a-EH-re-o. aereo is four syllables, a-EH-re-o.

variations.display: Ci vuole un'ora per arrivare in treno
variations.cue: It takes an hour to get there by train
variations.changed: how you travel

variations.display: Ci vuole un'ora in macchina
variations.cue: It takes an hour by car
variations.changed: the shortest form of the same answer

variations.display: Ci vuole poco per arrivare in aereo
variations.cue: It does not take long to get there by plane
variations.changed: an amount instead of a count, which keeps the singular

mistake.display: Ci vogliono un'ora per arrivare in aereo
mistake.why: One hour is one thing. The plural ci vogliono is for two or more, and mixing them up is the same error as ci vuole due ore in reverse.

sentences.mnemonic: One hour, one verb: ci vuole.

sentences.display: Gira a destra al semaforo, poi attraversa il ponte
sentences.cue: Turn right at the lights, then cross the bridge
sentences.literal: Turn at right at-the traffic-light, then cross the bridge

words.note: attraversare takes a direct object with no preposition: attraversa il ponte, attraversa la strada. English cross behaves the same way.

sentences.trap: L2-M4 gave these directions to a stranger, so they were giri and attraversi. Inside a story told to a friend they come out in tu, and only the ending moves.
sentences.sound: JEE-ra a DES-tra al se-MA-fo-ro, poy at-tra-VEHR-sa eel PON-te. attraversa is stressed on the VEHR.

variations.display: Gira a sinistra al semaforo, poi attraversa il ponte
variations.cue: Turn left at the lights, then cross the bridge
variations.changed: which way you turn

variations.display: Attraversa il ponte, poi gira a destra
variations.cue: Cross the bridge, then turn right
variations.changed: the order of the two moves

variations.display: Gira a destra, poi attraversa il ponte
variations.cue: Turn right, then cross the bridge
variations.changed: the landmark left out, as it is when the other person knows the road

mistake.display: Gira a destra al semaforo, poi attraversare il ponte
mistake.why: Both halves are orders, so both take the imperative. attraversare is the dictionary form and cannot carry a command on its own.

sentences.usage: Telling a friend how to reach you, in the middle of a story about getting there.

sentences.display: Ci siamo fermati in campagna, vicino a un lago
sentences.cue: We stopped in the countryside, near a lake
sentences.literal: Ourselves we-are stopped in countryside, near at a lake

words.note: fermarsi is reflexive, so it goes on essere and the participle agrees. A whole block: the ci is part of the verb, not a place word.
In campagna with no article, like al mare and in montagna. It means open country, not a political campaign.

sentences.trap: The ci here belongs to fermarsi and is not the ci of ci vuole. Two different jobs for the same two letters, and the verb tells you which.
sentences.sound: chee SYA-mo fer-MA-tee een kam-PA-nya, vee-CHEE-no a oon LA-go. campagna has the ny of canyon.

variations.display: Ci siamo fermati in campagna per due ore
variations.cue: We stopped in the countryside for two hours
variations.changed: how long instead of where exactly

variations.display: Ci siamo fermati vicino al lago
variations.cue: We stopped near the lake
variations.changed: one landmark instead of two

variations.display: Mi sono fermato in campagna, vicino a un lago
variations.cue: I stopped in the countryside, near a lake
variations.changed: one traveller, and the participle follows

mistake.display: Ci abbiamo fermato in campagna, vicino a un lago
mistake.why: A reflexive verb goes on essere. The shape is ci siamo fermati, with the participle agreeing with us, and abbiamo cannot appear in it.

sentences.usage: The middle of a story about a drive that took longer than planned.

sentences.display: Mi sono perso, ma ho trovato la strada
sentences.cue: I got lost, but I found the way
sentences.literal: Myself I-am lost, but I-have found the road

words.note: perdersi, reflexive and therefore on essere. A woman says mi sono persa; L2-M8's perso on its own is what you do to an object.

sentences.trap: The two halves take two auxiliaries. perdersi is reflexive and goes on essere; trovare is ordinary and goes on avere, in the same breath.
sentences.sound: mee SO-no PEHR-so, ma o tro-VA-to la STRA-da.

variations.display: Mi sono persa, ma ho trovato la strada
variations.cue: I got lost, but I found the way
variations.changed: a woman telling the same story

variations.display: Mi sono perso, ma ho trovato l'albergo
variations.cue: I got lost, but I found the hotel
variations.changed: what turned up in the end

variations.display: Mi sono perso in città
variations.cue: I got lost in town
variations.changed: the recovery left out

mistake.display: Ho perso, ma ho trovato la strada
mistake.why: ho perso means I lost something. Getting lost yourself is perdersi, and the reflexive brings essere with it: mi sono perso.

sentences.usage: Admitting it after arriving forty minutes late.
sentences.mnemonic: You lose a thing with ho; you lose yourself with sono.

sentences.display: Un biglietto di andata e ritorno, per favore
sentences.literal: A ticket of going and return, please

words.note: One fixed block at a ticket window, and the order never changes. On its own, andata is L1-M5's participle of andare and means something else entirely.
The journey home as a noun: il biglietto di ritorno, il ritorno è domani. The verb behind it is tornare, which is L1-M10's.

sentences.trap: andata e ritorno is one word for the purposes of buying a ticket, and the halves cannot be swapped. Ritorno e andata means nothing at a window.
sentences.sound: oon bee-LYET-to dee an-DA-ta e ree-TOR-no, per fa-VO-re. biglietto has the ly of million, bee-LYET-to.

variations.display: Un biglietto di andata e ritorno, grazie
variations.cue: A return ticket, thanks
variations.changed: the shorter courtesy

variations.display: Il biglietto di ritorno è per domani
variations.cue: The return ticket is for tomorrow
variations.changed: the noun on its own, without the fixed pair

variations.display: Ho comprato un biglietto di andata e ritorno
variations.cue: I bought a return ticket
variations.changed: reported afterwards instead of asked for at the window

mistake.display: Un biglietto di ritorno e andata, per favore
mistake.why: The order is fixed: andata e ritorno, out and then back. Reversed, it stops being the name of a ticket and becomes a description nobody uses.

sentences.usage: At the window, with a queue behind you.
sentences.mnemonic: Out first, back second — andata e ritorno.

sentences.display: Scendi qui, l'albergo è vicino al mare
sentences.cue: Get off here, the hotel is near the sea
sentences.literal: Get-down here, the-hotel is near at-the sea

words.cue: get off, go down (to a friend)
words.note: The opposite of salire, and the verb for getting off a bus or a train. On essere in the past: siamo scesi.
The elided l'albergo is its own surface and answers for nothing else. Masculine: un albergo, gli alberghi.

sentences.trap: The article does not vanish in front of a vowel, it elides: l'albergo. Writing albergo bare is a headline, not a sentence.
sentences.sound: SHEN-dee kwee, lal-BEHR-go eh vee-CHEE-no al MA-re. scendi opens with the sh of ship, SHEN-dee.

variations.display: Scendi qui, l'albergo è vicino al ponte
variations.cue: Get off here, the hotel is near the bridge
variations.changed: the landmark

variations.display: Scendiamo qui, l'albergo è vicino al mare
variations.cue: Let us get off here, the hotel is near the sea
variations.changed: both of you getting off

variations.display: Scendi al semaforo, l'albergo è vicino
variations.cue: Get off at the lights, the hotel is close by
variations.changed: where to get off, with the destination left vague

mistake.display: Scendi qui, albergo è vicino al mare
mistake.why: Italian keeps the article and elides it in front of a vowel. The surface is l'albergo, one token, apostrophe and all.

sentences.usage: Sending somebody off a bus one stop before yours.
sentences.mnemonic: l'albergo — the apostrophe is part of the word.

sentences.display: Ho fatto la valigia, partiamo verso mezzogiorno
sentences.cue: I have packed, we are leaving around midday
sentences.literal: I-have made the suitcase, we-leave towards midday

words.note: Fare la valigia is to pack — Italian MAKES the suitcase where English packs it, and the verb is always fare.
The present used for a plan, exactly as English we are leaving does. partire da is where from and partire per is where to.
Approximate: verso mezzogiorno, verso sera. For a place it means in the direction of, and it takes no article after it.

sentences.trap: Packing is fare la valigia, never impacchettare. And an approximate time takes verso, not circa, which counts quantities instead.
sentences.sound: o FAT-to la va-LEE-ja, par-TYA-mo VEHR-so med-zo-JOR-no. valigia is va-LEE-ja, with the j of jam.

variations.display: Ho fatto la valigia, partiamo verso sera
variations.cue: I have packed, we are leaving around evening
variations.changed: when

variations.display: Ho fatto la valigia, partiamo domani
variations.cue: I have packed, we are leaving tomorrow
variations.changed: a day instead of an hour, so verso goes

variations.display: Partiamo verso mezzogiorno, ho già fatto la valigia
variations.cue: We are leaving around midday — I have already packed
variations.changed: the plan first and the packing as reassurance

mistake.display: Ho fatto la valigia, partiamo circa mezzogiorno
mistake.why: circa counts things — circa venti persone. An approximate time of day is verso mezzogiorno, and the two are not interchangeable.

sentences.usage: Texting somebody the night before a trip.
sentences.mnemonic: verso a time, circa a number.

sentences.display: Che bella gita, siamo saliti in montagna a piedi
sentences.cue: What a lovely day out — we walked up into the mountains
sentences.literal: What beautiful outing, we-are gone-up in mountain at feet

words.note: A trip you come back from the same day, so it is not a viaggio. Fare una gita is the verb it goes with.
salire on essere when it means going up somewhere, so the participle agrees with us. It is also the verb for getting ON a bus.
In montagna with no article, matching al mare and in campagna. It names the whole kind of place, not one peak.

sentences.trap: salire goes on essere here, so the participle agrees. abbiamo salito appears only when the verb takes an object, which this sentence does not give it.
sentences.sound: ke BEL-la JEE-ta, SYA-mo sa-LEE-tee een mon-TA-nya a PYEH-dee.

variations.display: Che bella gita, siamo saliti in montagna in macchina
variations.cue: What a lovely day out — we drove up into the mountains
variations.changed: how you got up there

variations.display: Siamo saliti in montagna a piedi
variations.cue: We walked up into the mountains
variations.changed: the verdict dropped, leaving the bare account

variations.display: Che bella gita, siamo andati al lago
variations.cue: What a lovely day out — we went to the lake
variations.changed: where the day was spent

mistake.display: Che bella gita, abbiamo salito in montagna a piedi
mistake.why: With no object behind it, salire takes essere and its participle agrees: siamo saliti. abbiamo salito would need something climbed to be there.

sentences.usage: The line you send with the photographs on Sunday evening.
sentences.mnemonic: Up on your own feet, up on essere.
